requirement: The 12 V input is fused and protected against reverse polarity.
Every exposed neon lamp lead is sleeved with insulation rated at least 300 V (600 V preferred).
HV-side parts meet minimum ratings: CHV >=250 V; bleeder and sense resistors >=200 V; anode and lamp resistors 1 W.
A hung firmware loop resets the Nano within 2 s.
No Gerber or drill files are produced until a routed board passes native ERC and DRC and an experienced HV review is signed off.
Validation records keep recorded file checks separate from physical checks, and claim only what was done.
Six upright IN-14 tubes show HH MM SS, with an NE-2 separator between each pair.
12- or 24-hour display is selectable and remembered across power cycles.
Time can be set with the SET, H and M buttons and over USB serial.
The DS3231 keeps time on a CR2032 primary cell while unpowered (about +/-2 ppm, 0-40 C).
An optional sleep window blanks the display; any button wakes it for 30 s.
Once an hour every cathode of every tube is lit briefly (anti-poisoning).
The display stays off while the time is invalid (except while the user is setting it, 60 s timeout).
STATUS over serial reports time, VIN, HV, state, faults and button states.
With all digits lit the 12 V input current stays near 0.25 A (stop above 0.35 A); adapter rated >=1 A.
HV load with all six tubes and both lamps lit stays within the converter rating (model: about 35 % of 30 mA).
HV5522 logic supply stays within 10.8-13.2 V; firmware refuses HV outside that VIN window.
Heirloom case: printed inner case 234 x 80 x 112 mm clad in a mitred hardwood box 254 x 100 x 121.5 mm (129.5 mm on its feet), outer edges rounded R3.
Premium finish: hardwood (walnut by default) with an oil finish, a 1 mm brass bezel with six brass screws around the window, brass feet and brass button caps.
satisfied_by: wood_box(), brass_bezel(), brass_foot(), BOM_mechanical.csv wood and brass lines

requirement: Wood never carries a functional fit and never touches the electronics: every precise feature is in the printed inner case, and the wood is held only by four screws into its top board.
source: Design choice (forgiving woodwork, HV kept in the printed case)

requirement: Only M2 fasteners: 4x M2x16 (feet and floor to inner case), 4x M2x8 (inner case to wood top), 7x M2x6 (PCB, cable clamp), 6x M2x6 brass (bezel).
The tubes are fully enclosed: no glass passes through any opening; the case is lowered over the finished chassis.

All six numerals are seen through one front window glazed with a 3 mm smoked cast-acrylic panel, framed by the brass bezel and held by the floor and three silicone dots so it stays put when the case is lifted.
Every printed part fits a 256 x 256 x 256 mm build volume (Bambu Lab P1S); only the inner-case roof needs supports. The wood and brass parts are not printed.
With the case lifted off, TP1, TP4 and the HV_ARM shunt are reachable from the top of the chassis without reaching under the board.
satisfied_by: JP1, TP1-TP4 on the PCB top side (COMPONENT_PLACEMENT.csv)

requirement: SET, H and M are pressed from the top of the case through brass-coloured rods that rest on the switches by their own weight and are hidden from the window by a baffle.
The sealed, wood-clad case stays cool enough: modelled average internal rise about 3-5 K at about 2.7 W (wood insulation included); regulator checked at Stage 5.
PCB 218 x 64 x 1.6 mm, 4 layers, five M2 holes at the specified coordinates.
Built as cheaply as is safe: generic passives where allowed, no downgrades of safety items (planning total about $390 plus roughly $60-100 for wood and brass, not re-priced).
CI actions pinned by commit hash, least-privilege permissions, SBOM, SHA-256 checksums, Dependabot and CodeQL.
Every stage of the build guide lists parts, steps, measurements and PASS / FIX / STOP, with a safety gate before HV.
The project is published as a GitHub repository, a GitHub Pages website (installable offline) and a desktop app.
